ApplicabilityScope.description: Describes which nodes a parameter option can apply to. A node is in scope when it matches at least one value in every slot that is filled in; empty slots impose no restriction.

AppliedToEntity.description: A structured entity reference used by the CausalNode.applied_to slot. Uses the same entity_type / entity_term decomposition as CausalNode. Amounts (share, dominance, rank) do not belong here: they go on CompositionMember, in CausalNode.composition.

CausalEdge.description:
An edge in the labeled property graph representing a causal relationship. Carries all four annotation layers as properties:
  Layer 1: Claim strength and linguistic expression
  Layer 2: Philosophical account classification
  Layer 3: Sixteen causal features
  Layer 4: Evidential basis
Plus rendering metadata for each downstream target.

annotation_confidence.description: Annotator confidence in the overall annotation, 0.0-1.0.

annotation_notes.description: Free-text notes from the annotator about this edge.

annotation_timestamp.description: Date and time when the edge annotation was created.

annotator.description: Annotator identifier (human ORCID or model ID).

causal_language.description: How strong is the causal language used?

certainty_grade.description: GRADE-style certainty assessment for this individual causal claim. Controls downstream language in Rosetta Statement rendering.

comparator.description: What the effect described by this edge was assessed relative to. Answers "compared with what?" — a property of the causal inference, not an entity in the world, and therefore annotated here rather than as a control node. One entry per comparison arm, so designs with more than one contrast keep a separate description and comparator_node_id for each: a BACI design (e.g. Kramer et al. 1995) records one pre_treatment_baseline entry and one untreated_control or spatial_or_temporal_control entry. Use a single entry when the source reports one comparison.

context_dependence.description: Annotation of scope conditions or context dependence for the causal relationship.

contributing_sole.description: Whether the cause is presented as a sole cause or contributing cause.

determinism.description: Whether the causal relationship frames the underlying process as deterministic or indeterministic, or uses probability only to express epistemic uncertainty.

direction.description: Annotation of causal direction and evidence for direction.

dose.description: The level or range of the subject intervention or driver that this edge reports on, e.g. an initial planting density of 5 to 11 ramets/m2. Annotate one edge per reported level or range when the source reports results separately by dose; the nodes stay the same and only the dose differs. Leave empty when the source reports no dose. Dose is a condition of the claim, not part of the node, so it does not enter variable_key.

dose_level.description: The subject driver's level on an ordinal scale, for sources that name a level without quantifying it, e.g. "under heavy browsing pressure" or "at intermediate densities". Use alongside dose where the source gives both a name and a quantity, and alone where it gives only the name; a named level is the reason a QuantityValue with no number should never be built. Like dose, it is a condition of the claim rather than part of the node, so it does not enter variable_key.

ecosystem_context.description: The IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology Level 3 ecosystem functional group in which this causal relationship was observed, represented by an ELMO ecosystem type term. Use this edge-level field for the ecosystem setting of the causal claim.

evidential_basis.description: Annotation of the evidence type and evidence object supporting the claim.

fcm_weight.description: Numeric edge weight for Fuzzy Cognitive Map rendering. Range: -1.0 (strong negative) to +1.0 (strong positive). Stored at the state level: its sign is the predicate sign only, and the subject and object qualifiers are not applied, because they are part of each node's identity. A variable-level FCM multiplies this weight by the subject and object fcm_sign at render time (see the sign-composition rule in CausalPredicateEnum). Magnitude is derived from the predicate's fcm_default_weight, causal_language, and the strength annotation. Can be overridden by expert elicitation; record which in fcm_weight_source.

fcm_weight_source.description: How the FCM weight was determined.

id.description: Unique edge identifier.

mediation.description: Annotation of any mediating pathway between cause and effect.

moderation.description: Annotation of any moderator or effect modifier for the causal relationship.

necessity.description: Whether the cause is characterized as necessary for the effect.

negated.description: True if the source reports that the relationship does NOT hold — a null result. This is the canonical null-result encoding, and it is always paired with causal_language: no_relationship: negated is true if and only if causal_language is no_relationship. Leave the object node as it would be for a positive finding (the tested direction if stated, otherwise no qualifier); never encode a null result by giving the object node the qualifier "unchanged".

object.description: Node ID of the effect entity.

original_sentence.description: The full original sentence(s) from which this edge was extracted. Preserved for RAG retrieval and rendering validation.

philosophical_accounts.description: Which philosophical account(s) of causation does this claim invoke? A claim may invoke multiple accounts simultaneously.

predicate.description: Edge type from controlled vocabulary.

proportionality.description: Whether the cause is characterized at a proportional level of specificity.

proximate_distal.description: Whether the cause is positioned as proximate, distal, or both.

reversibility.description: Whether removing the cause is characterized as reversing the effect.

scope.description: What the claim is about: one case (assertional), some cases under stated conditions (contingent), typical cases (prototypical) or all cases (universal). Use instead of token_or_type. Most findings reported from a single study are assertional or contingent; general statements in an author's own voice are prototypical or universal.

source_document.description: Reference to an entry in CausalGraph.source_documents, by document_id.

specificity.description: Whether the causal relationship is characterized as specific to particular causes or effects.

stability.description: Whether the causal relationship is characterized as stable across contexts or conditions.

strength.description: Annotation of the reported strength or magnitude of the causal relationship.

subject.description: Node ID of the cause entity.

sufficiency.description: Whether the cause is characterized as sufficient for the effect.

temporal_extent.description: The temporal window over which this causal effect was observed. Distinct from the study period in source_document (when fieldwork was done): this captures the timescale of the causal relationship itself. E.g., "native recovery occurred within three growing seasons of invasive removal." Enables filtering by effect duration and analysis of whether effect sizes vary with observation window.

temporal_ordering.description: Whether temporal ordering between cause and effect is addressed.

CausalGraph.description: A labeled property graph of causal claims extracted from scientific literature. The top-level container for nodes and edges.

evidence_base_assessments.description: Derived evidence-base-level assessments over sets of article-level causal edges. These should be regenerated when new relevant CausalEdge records are added.

graph_id.description: Unique identifier for this graph or sub-graph.

nodes.description: All causal entities (causes, effects, mediators, moderators).

source_document.description: Bibliographic and study-level metadata for the source document from which this graph was extracted.

source_documents.description: All documents contributing to this graph. Edges reference entries here by document_id rather than carrying inline copies.

CausalGraph.title: CausalGraph

CausalNode.description:
A node in the labeled property graph representing a causally active ecological entity — specifically, a state or change in state of an environmental variable or process. Merges ELMO's entity structure (Alamenciak et al. 2025) with CAMO's annotation requirements.
Key design principle: causation in ecology is represented between states or changes in state, not between things alone. A taxon does not cause anything by itself; the causally relevant annotation concerns the state or change of an attribute of a taxon. Therefore each node decomposes into:

  entity: what thing (taxon, chemical, abiotic factor, process)
  attribute: what measurable property (abundance, cover, rate)
  qualifier: whether or how it changed (present, increased, etc.)

The human-readable 'name' is the composed form: "Increased abundance of Canis lupus". The structured fields allow decomposed querying: "show me all claims involving Canis lupus" or "all claims about abundance changes" or "all claims where abundance decreased."
This pattern corresponds to ELMO's subject/object value + derivative qualifier + state/change qualifier structure.
For taxon-specific measurements a two-path model applies. Single-taxon measurements use entity_type: taxon, with the NCBITaxon ID in entity_term and the measured property in measured_attribute — the taxon node is both organism and measurement and participates directly in causal edges. Multi-taxon aggregates and ecological guilds ("native species", "shade-tolerant species") use entity_type: composite_variable with one or more NCBITaxon IDs or free-text guild names in applied_to. Causal edges are never used for taxon-to-measurement links; applied_to is a queryable annotation field only.

annotator.description: Annotator identifier (human ORCID or model ID).

applied_to.description:
The entity or entities that this node is directed at, acts upon, or whose scope the measurement spans. Covers two roles depending on node type:
(1) Scope role (composite_variable; earlier annotations may use environmental_variable): one or more taxa or ecological guilds whose measurements are aggregated or grouped — for example, "richness of liverworts, Sphagnum, and true mosses" (list the NCBITaxon ID for each group) or "abundance of native species" (free text "native species", tracked in NAO). NCBITaxon IDs for higher-rank taxa enable downstream traversal to all taxon nodes sharing that ID without requiring a structural edge. Free-text values are accepted for functional groups and guilds with no NCBITaxon resolution (e.g., "native species", "shade-tolerant species", "invasive plants") and should be tracked in the project NAO list. Do not use on single-taxon nodes — use entity_type: taxon with the NCBITaxon ID in entity_term instead.
(2) Target role (environmental_process and management_intervention): the specific entity that the process or intervention is directed at or acts upon. Use when the node's meaning is only complete with reference to a target — for example, "herbivory on Sphagnum" or "invasive species removal of Alliaria petiolata".
Accepts any entity type (taxon, community, habitat, etc.) using the same entity_type / entity_term decomposition as CausalNode.

components.description: For management_intervention nodes that apply a mixture or package, what it contained: one entry per component, with the taxon or material in counted_entity and its rate in the value fields (e.g. a seed mix of ten species with seeding rates). Defines what the intervention was; do not annotate components as separate nodes or edges unless the source reports results for them separately. This records what was applied. What was observed in an assemblage goes in composition on a composite_variable node.

composition.description:
For composite_variable nodes, the reported composition of the assemblage: its members and how much of the whole each accounts for. Requires entity_type: composite_variable. Not part of variable_key.
Which slot to use. Where the source gives each member's share, or ranks the members, record a composition: a number goes in member.share, a ranking with no number in member.dominance or member.rank. Where the source only names the members, with no share and no ranking, there is no composition to record: list them in applied_to and put presence or disappearance in state_or_change_qualifier, which is what those slots are for. Every composition member must carry an amount in one of the three forms, so a bare membership list will be rejected here by design.
Use components, not composition, for what a management intervention applied, such as a seed mix and its rates.

embedding_text.description: Concatenated text used for generating the embedding vector. Typically: name + description + synonym list.

embedding_vector.description: Pre-computed embedding vector for RAG retrieval. Stored as serialized float array. Generated by the indexing pipeline, not by annotators.

entity_term.description: The core ecological entity as an ontology CURIE, or free text when no cached ontology term matches yet. This is the "what thing" — the taxon, chemical, abiotic factor, or process class, and is the authoritative ontology grounding for the node's entity. Corresponds to ELMO's subject_value / object_value slot. Examples: NCBITaxon:9612 (Canis lupus), CHEBI:24279 (glucosinolate), ENVO:01000253 (grassland). Secondary ontology crosswalks, if needed, should be maintained outside article annotations in SSSOM files.

entity_type.description: High-level category of the ecological entity, for semantic disambiguation.

id.description: Unique node identifier. This field is populated automatically by the annotation tool; annotators do not need to fill it in. If entity_term is provided, Loom uses that CURIE; otherwise, Loom generates causal_mosaic:{slugified_name}_{4-char-hash}.

life_stage.description: The life stage of the organism this node measures, as a coarse facet. Kept out of measured_attribute, which is for the measured quality and is part of variable_key: a stage recorded there makes "abundance of seedlings" and "abundance of year 2 rosettes" two different variables for the wrong reason, and breaks the PATO grounding measured_attribute carries. Give mixed_or_whole_population for an unstaged count rather than leaving this empty.

life_stage_term.description: The stage as an ontology CURIE where one fits, otherwise as the source's own wording. For plants use a PO development-stage term under PO:0009012 - PO:0007131 (seedling development stage), not PO:0008037 (seedling), which is a structure rather than a stage. For animals use a UBERON life-cycle-stage term under UBERON:0000105. Free text is for distinctions neither ontology nor the enum keeps, e.g. "year 1 rosette" against "year 2 rosette".

measured_attribute.description: The measurable attribute of the entity that participates in the causal relationship. Corresponds to ELMO's derivative_qualifier slot. Together with entity_term and state_or_change_qualifier, forms the full semantic content: "state or change qualifier of attribute of entity." This is the authoritative ontology grounding for the measured attribute. Use PATO terms for qualities (abundance, density, cover, height), GO terms for process rates, or free text if no ontology term exists.

name.description: Human-readable composed label for the node. Should express the full semantic content: "Increased wolf population abundance" or "Prescribed burning process" or "Elevated soil nitrogen." This is what appears in Rosetta Statements and graph visualizations.

nativeness_basis.description: For nodes whose applied_to names native or non-native species, how nativeness was assigned.

parameter_options.description: Ways the state or change this node represents could be measured or supplied as a parameter, given as ids of ParameterOption entries in a ParameterOptionCatalog. A list of possibilities, independent of any source document: it does not record what a study measured. Used to bind nodes to data streams in digital twins and to choose observable variables when building causal models. Options apply to the variable, so nodes sharing a variable_key should carry the same options, filtered to those whose value_type suits the node's qualifier family.

source_spans.description: Text spans grounding this node in the source document.

spatial_grain.description: For environmental_variable nodes, the area of the sampling unit the measurement was made on, e.g. 1 m2 quadrats. Matters most for area-dependent attributes such as species richness. Not part of variable_key.

state_or_change_qualifier.description: Qualifier indicating the state or change in the attribute, including cases where the attribute is present, absent, or unchanged. "unchanged" describes a reported stable state, not a null result; null results are encoded on the edge (see CausalEdge.negated). Corresponds to ELMO's direction_qualifier slot. Combined with entity_term and measured_attribute to produce the node's full meaning: e.g., entity=Canis lupus, attribute=abundance, qualifier=increased gives "increased abundance of Canis lupus."

variable_key.description: A calculated key for the causal node to assist  in BBN variable grouping.

CausalNode.title: CausalNode

CausalPredicateEnum.description:
Controlled predicate vocabulary for causal edges, grounded primarily in CAMO and cross-linked to Biolink / RO where possible. Each predicate carries a sign and transitivity property for FCM rendering.
FCM sign composition. The predicate's sign annotation and the nodes' fcm_sign annotations (StateOrChangeQualifierEnum) combine by one of two conventions, chosen once per rendering and never mixed:
(1) State level: FCM concepts are CAMO nodes as annotated ("decreased X" and "increased X" are different concepts). Edge sign = predicate sign. Node qualifiers are not applied; they are already part of each concept's identity. CausalEdge.fcm_weight is stored at this level.
(2) Variable level: nodes are first collapsed to variables (entity + measured_attribute, qualifier dropped). Edge sign = subject fcm_sign x predicate sign x object fcm_sign, with positive = +1 and negative = -1. A node with no qualifier counts as +1, as do the process_phase values occurred and ongoing (fcm_sign neutral), since the node is the variable's reference state. An edge with an unchanged node on either end has no variable-level sign and is left out.
Worked examples, variable level: "increased X prevents Y" = (+1)(-1)(+1) = negative; "decreased X causes Y" = (-1)(+1)(+1) = negative (the same finding, same sign); "decreased X causes decreased Y" = (-1)(+1)(-1) = positive; "removed X disrupts increased Y" = (-1)(-1)(+1) = positive. Applying node signs at the state level, or using only the object sign at the variable level, flips edges.
Only predicates whose sign is positive or negative carry an FCM sign. unspecified, variable, pathway, modifier and temporal predicates need an explicit fcm_weight or are left out of the FCM. Negated edges (null results, causal_language: no_relationship) produce no FCM arc.
CausalPredicateEnum.title: CausalPredicateEnum

CausalPredicateQualifiers.description: The predicate layer of a causal statement: the philosophical account invoked and the causal features of the asserted relation. A simple predicate (camo:prevents) plus these qualifiers, following the Biolink pattern, because an RDF predicate is a single IRI. Fields mirror CAMO CausalEdge Layers 2-3; 'direction' and 'strength' are renamed to avoid colliding with SEPIO's evidential direction and strength.
CausalPredicateQualifiers.title: CausalPredicateQualifiers

CausalProposition.description: A proposition put forward by causal statements.

description.description: A free text description of the Entity.

extensions.description: A list of extensions to the Entity, that allow for capture of information not directly supported by elements defined in the model.

id.description: The 'logical' identifier of the entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID.  This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference one object from another.

identifiers.description: A globally-unique 'business' identifier or accession number for the real-world entity represented by a data object. These are typically assigned by an external system or authority, and used to connect entities and share content across different systems.

identity_key.description: The normalized key that defines this proposition under the identity rule.

identity_rule_version.description: Which identity rule produced this grouping. Changing the rule regroups statements, so it must be recorded.

label.description: A primary name for the Entity.

negated.description: A boolean flag set to 'true' to represent a negation of the proposition expressed by the subject, predicate, object, and qualifier(s) (e.g. that "Variant X is NOT pathogenic for Disease Y")

object.description: An Entity or concept that is related to the subject of a Proposition via its predicate.

predicate.description: The relationship declared to hold between the subject and the object of the Proposition.

propositionText.description: A natural-language expression of the Proposition's meaning (i.e. the 'possible fact' it expresses).

qualifier.description: An additional piece of information that extends or refines the meaning of a Propositions's core subject - predicate - object 'triple' - by providing additional detail, or constraining the statement to apply in a particular context.

raised_as_question.description: True if people created this proposition as an open question before any statement asserted it. Such propositions keep their id and are never deleted by re-derivation; they revert to open_question if their statements are removed.

scope.description: Semantic unit type of what is stated or proposed. Part of a proposition's identity; copied onto statements so propositions can be derived from them.

subject.description: The Entity or concept about which the Proposition is made.

type.description: The name of the class that is instantiated by a data object representing the Entity.

CausalProposition.title: CausalProposition

CausalStatement.description: A statement that one ecological state, change or process makes a causal (or associational) difference to another. Subject and object are CAMO node shapes; the predicate is a CAMO predicate, refined by the causal features in predicate_qualifiers.

camo_edge_id.description: Identifier of the CAMO CausalEdge this statement was migrated or projected from.

care.description: Consent, access and governance metadata. Required for statements whose author is an Indigenous knowledge holder or community member (checked by scripts/check_statements.py).

causal_language.description: How strongly the causal wording commits (statement-level hedging).

comparator.description: What the effect was assessed relative to.

context.description: Conditions under which the statement is said to hold (scope conditions), as the source gives them. Shared by every predicate group.

contributions.description: Who made the statement: at least one contribution with role author. Who recorded it goes in recordMetadata, not here.

dateAuthored.description: Indicates when the information content expressed in the Information Entity was generated.

derivedFrom.description: Another Information Entity from which this Information Entity is derived, in whole or in part.

description.description: A free text description of the Entity.

direction.description: A term indicating whether the Statement supports, disputes, or remains neutral w.r.t. the validity of the Proposition it evaluates.

dose.description: The reported level or range of the subject intervention or driver, using CAMO's quantity type. A condition of this statement, not a node definition or part of proposition identity.

dose_level.description: The subject driver's reported ordinal level. Use alone for a named level without a number, or with dose when the source supplies both. A condition of this statement, not part of proposition identity.

ecosystem_context.description: The KIND of ecosystem the statement is about, as one of CAMO's IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology functional groups (warm_temperate_forests, coastal_saltmarshes_and_reedbeds). Not a place: "Florida" or "the Mediterranean coast of Israel" go in `place` (R19).

extensions.description: A list of extensions to the Entity, that allow for capture of information not directly supported by elements defined in the model.

hasEvidence.description: A piece of information that represents or contributes to an argument for or against the validity of the Proposition put forth in a Statement. This is a shortcut relation that links a Statement directly to a piece of evidence supporting it, bypassing the Evidence Line class when used data creators do not utilize an Evidence Line object.

hasEvidenceFromSources.description: An Information Entity (typically a publication, dataset, or database) that provided information used as evidence to generate the knowledge expressed in a Statement.

hasEvidenceLines.description: An evidence-based argument that supports or disputes the validity of the proposition that a Statement assesses or puts forth as true. The strength and direction of this argument (whether it supports or disputes  the proposition, and how strongly) is based on an interpretation of one or more pieces of information as evidence (i.e. 'Evidence Items).

hasEvidenceOfTypes.description: A term describing a type of evidence used to assess the validity of Statement's proposition (e.g. 'sequence similarity evidence', 'in vitro assay evidence').

id.description: The 'logical' identifier of the entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID.  This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference one object from another.

identifiers.description: A globally-unique 'business' identifier or accession number for the real-world entity represented by a data object. These are typically assigned by an external system or authority, and used to connect entities and share content across different systems.

informationQuality.description: A qualitative term indicating the scientific rigor or reliability with which the information was generated/collected.

isAbout.description: An entity or concept in the world that the information entity describes/is about.

label.description: A primary name for the Entity.

modality.description: Whether the statement reports (observed), infers (inferred) or forecasts (anticipated). Different from hedging, which is causal_language: hedging is how sure the speaker sounds, modality is what kind of statement it is. A proposition projects to OWL only when every statement grouped under it is observed (decision D15).

negated.description: True if the statement asserts that the relationship does NOT hold (a null result). Same convention as CAMO: negated is true iff causal_language is no_relationship.

object.description: An Entity or concept that is related to the subject of a Statement via its predicate.

original_text.description: The statement as worded in its source (verbatim sentence, notebook line, transcript passage). Distinct from statementText, which is the normalized rendering.

ComparatorAnnotation.description:
One comparison arm of a causal edge; an edge lists one per arm (see CausalEdge.comparator). Controls are recorded here rather than as nodes: nodes represent states and changes in state, whereas a control represents what a measurement was contrasted with. Modelling a control as a node forces either a hub node shared across unrelated studies or a per-study singleton that can never merge, and neither survives type-level synthesis.
Where the comparison arm is itself a management decision a practitioner could take — natural regeneration, cessation of grazing — annotate it as an ordinary management_intervention or environmental_process node and point comparator_node_id at it. An arm that exists only to be measured against gets no node.
A factor applied to every arm including the comparator explains no between-arm difference and is not a cause the study tests; it should not be annotated as a cause in that document's graph.

comparator_description.description: The comparison arm as the source names it, verbatim or near-verbatim. E.g. "natural (disturbed, unseeded)", "no treatment (control)".

comparator_dose.description: The level or range of the subject driver in this comparison arm, so that both ends of the contrast are recoverable. Pairs with CausalEdge.dose, which gives this edge's own level: the two together are what lets a dose-response curve be fitted and an effect size be recomputed. Expected when comparator_type is alternative_dose_level.

comparator_dose_level.description: The arm's level on the ordinal scale, for sources that name it without a number, e.g. "relative to lower initial densities". Use alongside comparator_dose where the source gives both.

comparator_node_id.description: Node ID of the comparison arm, where that arm is itself annotated as a node. Expected when comparator_type is passive_management_arm or alternative_treatment; normally empty otherwise.

comparator_type.description: The basis against which the effect was assessed.

status.description: Assertion status for the comparator annotation.

ComparatorTypeEnum.description: The basis against which the effect described by an edge was assessed — what the claim is relative to. Experimental controls are recorded here rather than as nodes. A control is not a state or change in state, so it fails the CausalNode test, but it is not neutral either: the same reported effect means different things measured against untreated plots, against undisturbed remnant, or against the same plots before treatment.

CompositionAnnotation.description: The reported composition of an observed assemblage: which members make it up and how much of it each accounts for. Attaches to a CausalNode whose entity is a composite_variable, and describes that node's entity rather than a causal relationship. Distinct from CausalNode.components, which records what a management intervention applied (a seed mix and its rates); this records what was observed. Members are usually taxa but need not be: a fraction of particulate organic matter by biomass is a member too. Not modelled: a ratio between two groups ("forb-to-grass ratio 3.5:1"), and nesting of groups within groups (list the leaf members and let the flat list stand).

basis.description: What the member shares measure. Required, because a share without its basis cannot be compared across studies.

members.description: The members of the assemblage, one entry each.

total_share.description: The share of the whole that the listed members jointly account for, where the source states it, e.g. "comprised more than 87% of the cladoceran assemblage" is minimum_value 87. Records that the list is partial without forcing an invented remainder.

CompositionMember.description: One member of an observed assemblage, with how much of the whole it accounts for. Inherits the entity_type / entity_term / life_stage decomposition from EntityReference, so a member is grounded the same way as an applied_to entry, and adds the member's amount. Give share when the source reports a number, dominance when it ranks members without one, and rank to preserve an explicit ordering.

entity_term.description: The target entity as an ontology CURIE (preferred) or free text. For taxa use NCBITaxon where available, otherwise Wikidata QIDs; for environments ENVO; for processes GO.

entity_type.description: High-level category of the target entity.

rank.description: The member's position in an ordering the source states explicitly, 1 for the first named, e.g. "detected most frequently, followed by coyotes and lynx". Independent of list order.

share.description: How much of the whole this member accounts for, in the units named by CompositionAnnotation.basis. Use the QuantityValue range fields for a reported range, e.g. "2-6% relative abundance" is minimum_value 2 and maximum_value 6.

CriteriaSet.description: One body's versioned definition of a concept such as "degraded area": a particular, but an information record, not a node. A stated, versioned test that criteria statements apply, described only by a fixed set of definitional elements plus its verbatim text, so a definition never becomes its own small graph. Taxa, indicator variables and measured values never appear here: they belong in the evidence for a criteria statement. Deliberately not an OWL definition, so a verdict can never be inferred, and a definition can change without any record being rewritten.

CriteriaStatement.description: That a site or project meets (or does not meet) a named, versioned definition, for an assessed period. The subject is a particular: a site individual (degradation) or a project individual (effectiveness), so no subject_proposition and no exactly_one_of rule (decision D17; R7 and R18 go away). The verdict is the statement's evidential direction (supports, disputes, neutral) and is required: criteria statements are the one annotated statement that fills it. "Degraded" with no definition named is context, not a criteria statement. Annotator's test: is someone applying a named, versioned definition to a site or project?

NodeDefinition.description: Says which node template a node fills and with which terms. The CAMO node stays the annotation record; this is its logical definition.

depth.description: A refinement (templates' `refinements`): the depth interval the node is about, e.g. 0 to 15 cm. Part of what the node is, but with no ontology class, so the node is a subclass of the template's expression rather than equivalent to it. Only for templates that list it (quality_of_environmental_material).

fillers.description: One filler per template variable. Required for class_expression templates (checked by scripts/expand_nodes.py); strategies and sites have no variables.

season.description: A refinement: the season the node is about ("growing season", "spring freshet"). As for depth.

template.description: Id of a template in templates/node_templates.yaml.

NodeDefinition.title: NodeDefinition

ParameterOption.description: One way of measuring or supplying a value for a node: a type of sensor, survey, assay, record or model, described independently of any study. Many nodes can share one option (e.g. quadrat percent cover applies to any plant cover node). An option says what could be measured, not what was measured.

acquisition_method.description: Broad kind of data collection the option uses.

id.description: Unique identifier for the option, in the camo_param namespace (e.g. camo_param:quadrat_percent_cover). Stable once published, since nodes refer to it.

label.description: Short human-readable name (e.g. "Percent cover in fixed quadrats", "NDVI from Sentinel-2 imagery").

measurement_relation.description: Whether the option measures the node's attribute directly, measures a proxy for it, or derives it from other quantities.

observable_property.description: What the option actually measures, as a CURIE (preferred) or free text. Required for proxy and derived options; for direct options it may be left empty, meaning the node's own measured_attribute. Prefer I-ADOPT variables, NVS P01 parameters, ECSO measurement types or EnvThes terms.

option_description.description: Fuller explanation of the option: what is recorded, typical deployment, and known limitations.

protocol.description: A standard method this option follows, as a DOI, URL or CURIE, or free text naming it (e.g. a GEO BON protocol, an LTER method, a protocols.io entry).

scope.description: Which kinds of node the option can apply to. Used to narrow the candidates when matching options to nodes, and to document intent.

sensor_or_instrument.description: The instrument or device class used, as a CURIE (preferred) or free text. Prefer NVS L05 device categories or L22 instrument terms. Leave empty for methods with no instrument (e.g. expert_elicitation).

typical_spatial_resolution_m.description: Typical spatial grain in metres (pixel size, plot or quadrat side, or sensor footprint).

typical_temporal_resolution.description: Typical interval between successive values, as an ISO 8601 duration (e.g. PT15M, P1D, P1Y).

unit.description: Unit of the values the option produces, as a QUDT unit (preferred) or UO term. Leave empty for unitless, binary or categorical values.

value_type.description: The kind of value the option produces.

ParameterOption.title: ParameterOption

ParameterOptionCatalog.description: A versioned registry of parameter options: the sensor, survey, assay, record and model types that can measure or supply CAMO nodes. Kept in its own file and shared by all graphs; nodes refer to its entries by id through CausalNode.parameter_options.

catalog_version.description: Version of the catalog contents, changed whenever options are added, edited or deprecated. Independent of the schema version.

options.description: The parameter options in this catalog.

schema_version.description: CAMO schema version the catalog conforms to.

ParameterOptionCatalog.title: ParameterOptionCatalog

Period.description: A calendar period. CAMO's TemporalExtent has no start or end, so this is a separate class (R2). Start and end are ISO 8601 strings at whatever granularity the source gives: a year (2023), a year and month (2024-05) or a full date (2026-03-31). An absent end means open or ongoing. Exporters write normalized xsd:dateTime bounds beside the verbatim strings; xsd:date, xsd:gYear and xsd:duration never reach a generated file, because they are not in the OWL 2 datatype map (decision D19). Overlap is computed on the bounds (scripts/warp_time.py), never by comparing strings.

end.description: ISO 8601 year, year-month or date. Absent if open or ongoing.

Period.title: Period

PhilosophicalAccountEnum.description: The philosophical account of causation invoked by a causal claim, per Illari and Russo's (2014) mosaic. Each account offers a different lens on what it means for C to cause E.
PhilosophicalAccountEnum.title: PhilosophicalAccountEnum

Proposition.description: An abstract entity representing a possible fact that is either true or false.

description.description: A free text description of the Entity.

extensions.description: A list of extensions to the Entity, that allow for capture of information not directly supported by elements defined in the model.

id.description: The 'logical' identifier of the entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID.  This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference one object from another.

identifiers.description: A globally-unique 'business' identifier or accession number for the real-world entity represented by a data object. These are typically assigned by an external system or authority, and used to connect entities and share content across different systems.

label.description: A primary name for the Entity.

negated.description: A boolean flag set to 'true' to represent a negation of the proposition expressed by the subject, predicate, object, and qualifier(s) (e.g. that "Variant X is NOT pathogenic for Disease Y")

object.description: An Entity or concept that is related to the subject of a Proposition via its predicate.

predicate.description: The relationship declared to hold between the subject and the object of the Proposition.

propositionText.description: A natural-language expression of the Proposition's meaning (i.e. the 'possible fact' it expresses).

qualifier.description: An additional piece of information that extends or refines the meaning of a Propositions's core subject - predicate - object 'triple' - by providing additional detail, or constraining the statement to apply in a particular context.

subject.description: The Entity or concept about which the Proposition is made.

type.description: The name of the class that is instantiated by a data object representing the Entity.

Proposition.title: Proposition

PropositionStatusEnum.description: Whether anyone has asserted the proposition yet.
PropositionStatusEnum.title: PropositionStatusEnum

ProximateDistalEnum.description: Whether the cause is positioned as proximate, distal, or both.
ProximateDistalEnum.title: ProximateDistalEnum

Qualifier.description: A key-value object used to capture additional piece of information that extends or refines the meaning of a Statement's core subject - predicate - object 'triple' - by providing additional detail, or constraining the statement to apply in a particular context.

name.description: A descriptive name that describes the type of information captured in the Qualifier value.

value.description: The value of the qualifier - holding information that refines/extends the meaning of the Statement.

Qualifier.title: Qualifier

QualifierFamilyEnum.description: Groups StateOrChangeQualifierEnum values into mutually exclusive families. A set of qualifiers forms a valid state space only if all members share a family.
QualifierFamilyEnum.title: QualifierFamilyEnum

Quantity.description: A number with a unit. Where a proposal sketch says QuantityValue, it means this (R1). A count of things (46 protected areas) is a Count, not a Quantity: "protected area" is not a unit.

unit.description: The unit, as a CURIE: UO (numeric IDs: UO:0000008, never UO:hectare), QUDT (unit:), a scale scheme (scale:) when the number is a position on a source's scale, or a TODO: placeholder.

Quantity.title: Quantity

QuantityRange.description: An interval with a unit. Either end may be absent (one-sided ranges: "tolerates pH above 5.5"), but not both. When both are present, min is at most max (checked by scripts/check_values.py).
QuantityRange.title: QuantityRange

QuantityValue.description: A reported quantity: a single value or a range, its unit, and the entity being counted or measured. Used for intervention doses (CausalEdge.dose), intervention components (CausalNode.components) and sampling grain (CausalNode.spatial_grain). Give numeric_value for a single value, or minimum_value and/or maximum_value for a range or threshold ("5 or more" is minimum_value 5 with no maximum).

counted_entity.description: What is counted or measured, when the unit alone does not say, e.g. ramets of Sanguinaria canadensis in "9 ramets/m2".

maximum_value.description: Upper bound of a reported range, inclusive.

minimum_value.description: Lower bound of a reported range or threshold, inclusive.

unit.description: Unit of the value, as a QUDT unit (preferred) or UO term, matching ParameterOption.unit. For counts per area give the area unit (e.g. per square metre) and name what is counted in counted_entity. Leave empty for unitless counts, and when no QUDT or UO term fits (ecological density units such as ramets/m2 or deer/km2 often have none): put the source's own wording in unit_text instead.

unit_text.description: The unit as the source words it, for use only when no QUDT or UO term exists for it, e.g. "ramets/m2" or "deer/km2". unit stays an identifier; this slot makes the fallback explicit so a consumer can tell a resolvable unit from a free-text one. Do not fill it when unit is set. Differs from verbatim, which is the whole quantity (value and unit), not the unit alone.

verbatim.description: The quantity as the source states it, e.g. '9 and 11 ramets/m2'.

QuantityValue.title: QuantityValue

RecommendationPredicateEnum.description: The recommendation group's one predicate. warp:suggested_to is abstract in the relation layer: the exporter always writes the sub-property the statement's guidance selects (decision D16), declared in src/warp/owl/warp-relations.ttl.
RecommendationPredicateEnum.title: RecommendationPredicateEnum

RecommendationProposition.description: A proposition put forward by recommendation statements: this guidance, about this action, for this outcome, at this scope. Two agencies giving the same guidance share one; "do" and "avoid" for the same action and outcome are two, which may cite the same causal proposition: agreement about how the world works, disagreement about what to do.

description.description: A free text description of the Entity.

extensions.description: A list of extensions to the Entity, that allow for capture of information not directly supported by elements defined in the model.

id.description: The 'logical' identifier of the entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID.  This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference one object from another.

identifiers.description: A globally-unique 'business' identifier or accession number for the real-world entity represented by a data object. These are typically assigned by an external system or authority, and used to connect entities and share content across different systems.

identity_key.description: The normalized key that defines this proposition under the identity rule.

identity_rule_version.description: Which identity rule produced this grouping. Changing the rule regroups statements, so it must be recorded.

label.description: A primary name for the Entity.

negated.description: A boolean flag set to 'true' to represent a negation of the proposition expressed by the subject, predicate, object, and qualifier(s) (e.g. that "Variant X is NOT pathogenic for Disease Y")

object.description: An Entity or concept that is related to the subject of a Proposition via its predicate.

predicate.description: The relationship declared to hold between the subject and the object of the Proposition.

predicate_qualifiers.description: The identity extra this proposition was grouped by (guidance).

propositionText.description: A natural-language expression of the Proposition's meaning (i.e. the 'possible fact' it expresses).

qualifier.description: An additional piece of information that extends or refines the meaning of a Propositions's core subject - predicate - object 'triple' - by providing additional detail, or constraining the statement to apply in a particular context.

raised_as_question.description: True if people created this proposition as an open question before any statement asserted it. Such propositions keep their id and are never deleted by re-derivation; they revert to open_question if their statements are removed.

scope.description: Semantic unit type of what is stated or proposed. Part of a proposition's identity; copied onto statements so propositions can be derived from them.

subject.description: The Entity or concept about which the Proposition is made.

type.description: The name of the class that is instantiated by a data object representing the Entity.

RecommendationProposition.title: RecommendationProposition

RecommendationQualifiers.description: The predicate layer of a recommendation statement. Only guidance is in the identity key; force, priority, timing and contribution vary across the statements of one proposition.

contribution.description: Direct, or a precursor to actions that act on the outcome.

deontic_force.description: How strongly the guidance binds: required (a legal duty), recommended, suggested, optional.

guidance.description: Do, avoid or consider. In the identity key.

priority.description: The priority on the source's own scale (DFO High / Medium / Low; ECCC Urgent / Necessary / Beneficial), as a ScaledValue with scale and concept IRIs from vocab/scales.yaml.

timing_of_influence.description: When the action takes effect, on the source's scale (DFO Immediate / Medium / Future).

RecommendationQualifiers.title: RecommendationQualifiers

RecommendationStatement.description: Guidance: a source tells someone to do, avoid or consider an action because of an outcome. The subject is the action as the source names it (an action node, or a management strategy node), never the recommender: who gave the advice is the claimant (the author contribution), as in every group. The object is the outcome node, a change or target state. The advice is in predicate_qualifiers.guidance. Annotator's test: is the source telling someone what to do, or describing what happens? Describing is a causal statement.

care.description: Consent, access and governance metadata. Required for statements whose author is an Indigenous knowledge holder or community member (checked by scripts/check_statements.py).

context.description: Conditions under which the statement is said to hold (scope conditions), as the source gives them. Shared by every predicate group.

contributions.description: Who made the statement: at least one contribution with role author. Who recorded it goes in recordMetadata, not here.

dateAuthored.description: Indicates when the information content expressed in the Information Entity was generated.

derivedFrom.description: Another Information Entity from which this Information Entity is derived, in whole or in part.

description.description: A free text description of the Entity.

direction.description: A term indicating whether the Statement supports, disputes, or remains neutral w.r.t. the validity of the Proposition it evaluates.

ecosystem_context.description: The KIND of ecosystem the statement is about, as one of CAMO's IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology functional groups (warm_temperate_forests, coastal_saltmarshes_and_reedbeds). Not a place: "Florida" or "the Mediterranean coast of Israel" go in `place` (R19).

extensions.description: A list of extensions to the Entity, that allow for capture of information not directly supported by elements defined in the model.

hasEvidence.description: A piece of information that represents or contributes to an argument for or against the validity of the Proposition put forth in a Statement. This is a shortcut relation that links a Statement directly to a piece of evidence supporting it, bypassing the Evidence Line class when used data creators do not utilize an Evidence Line object.

hasEvidenceFromSources.description: An Information Entity (typically a publication, dataset, or database) that provided information used as evidence to generate the knowledge expressed in a Statement.

hasEvidenceLines.description: An evidence-based argument that supports or disputes the validity of the proposition that a Statement assesses or puts forth as true. The strength and direction of this argument (whether it supports or disputes  the proposition, and how strongly) is based on an interpretation of one or more pieces of information as evidence (i.e. 'Evidence Items).

hasEvidenceOfTypes.description: A term describing a type of evidence used to assess the validity of Statement's proposition (e.g. 'sequence similarity evidence', 'in vitro assay evidence').

id.description: The 'logical' identifier of the entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID.  This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference one object from another.

identifiers.description: A globally-unique 'business' identifier or accession number for the real-world entity represented by a data object. These are typically assigned by an external system or authority, and used to connect entities and share content across different systems.

informationQuality.description: A qualitative term indicating the scientific rigor or reliability with which the information was generated/collected.

isAbout.description: An entity or concept in the world that the information entity describes/is about.

justified_by.description: The propositions the guidance cites as its reason, usually causal propositions ("avoid stocking: stocking decreases abundance"). Empty when the source gives no reason. A prediction in the guidance is recorded as its own causal statement (modality anticipated) and cited here; it is never derived from the guidance automatically.

label.description: A primary name for the Entity.

modality.description: Whether the statement reports (observed), infers (inferred) or forecasts (anticipated). Different from hedging, which is causal_language: hedging is how sure the speaker sounds, modality is what kind of statement it is. A proposition projects to OWL only when every statement grouped under it is observed (decision D15).

object.description: The outcome: a change or target state.

original_text.description: The statement as worded in its source (verbatim sentence, notebook line, transcript passage). Distinct from statementText, which is the normalized rendering.

place.description: The REGION the statement is about, as an IRI from a registered place scheme: an ISO 3166-2 code for a province or state (ISO3166-2:CA-SK); a Wikidata item for a municipality, park, lake or territory (wd:Q...); a GeoNames or Getty TGN entry where Wikidata has none; an ENVO ecoregion individual; or, failing all of these, a locally minted place: concept with a TODO to replace it. Never a bare name, never a coordinate pair standing in for an area. Not the kind of ecosystem, which is ecosystem_context. Part of the identity key for tolerance and cost statements (decision D18). How to find an IRI: docs/values.md.

predicate.description: The relationship declared to hold between the subject and the object of the Statement.

predicate_qualifiers.description: The guidance, its force, priority, timing and contribution.

proposition.description: The proposition this statement puts forward. DERIVED: filled by scripts/derive_propositions.py, never by annotators. Exception: SynthesisAssessment, which targets a chosen proposition.

qualifier.description: An additional piece of information that extends or refines the meaning of a Statement's core subject - predicate - object 'triple' - by providing additional detail, or constraining the statement to apply in a particular context.

recordMetadata.description: Provenance of this record: who annotated it in EcoWeaver and when (role annotator, dateRecordCreated).

reportedIn.description: The source documents the statement was reported in, by id.

scope.description: Semantic unit type of what is stated or proposed. Part of a proposition's identity; copied onto statements so propositions can be derived from them.

score.description: A quantitative score that indicates the strength of a Proposition's validity assessment in the direction indicated (i.e. how strongly supported or disputed the Proposition is believed to be).  Depending on its implementation, a score may reflect how *confident* that agent is that the Proposition is true or false, or the *strength of evidence* they believe supports or disputes it.

source_spans.description: Text spans grounding the statement in its source document.

sources.description: A document or other informtion resource in which the information entity, or evidence supporting it, is reported.

specifiedBy.description: A specification that describes all or part of the process that led to creation of the Information Entity.

specified_in.description: Plan documents that specify what was, or is to be, done: a recovery strategy, a restoration plan, a work order. Referenced by id, not inlined. Used by strategies and implementation statements.

statementText.description: A natural-language expression of what a Statement asserts to be true.

strength.description: A term used to report the strength of a Proposition's assessment in the direction indicated (i.e. how strongly supported or disputed the Proposition is believed to be).  Implementers may choose to frame a strength assessment in terms of how *confident* an agent is that the Proposition is true or false, or in terms of the *strength of all evidence* they believe supports or disputes it.

subject.description: The action, or strategy, as the source names it.

subjectClassification.description: A single term or phrase summarizing the outcome of direction and strength assessments of a Statement's proposition, in terms of a classification of its subject.

supportingMethodTypes.description: Types of methodological approaches that were executed to directly or indirectly support creation of the Information Entity.

supportingMethods.description: Specific methods that were executed to directly or indirectly support creation of the Information Entity.

temporal_extent.description: The temporal window over which the stated effect or condition was observed (CAMO TemporalExtent). Not a calendar period: dated periods use Period (start and end as ISO 8601 strings).

type.description: The name of the class that is instantiated by a data object representing the Entity.

RecommendationStatement.title: RecommendationStatement

RecordMetadata.description: A reusable structure that encapsulates provenance metadata about a serialized data record or object in a particular dataset (as opposed to provenance of the real world entity this record or object represents).

contributions.description: describes specific contributions made by an human or software agent to the creation, modification, or administrative management of a data record or object.

dateRecordCreated.description: The date the record was initially created.

derivedFromRecord.description: Another data record from which the record described here was derived, through a data ingest and/or transformation process.

recordIdentifier.description: The identifier of the record described in the RecordMetadata object (required when the record described is not the one in the present system).

recordVersion.description: The version number of the record-level artifact the object describes.

RecordMetadata.title: RecordMetadata

Recurrence.description: A repeating strategy component: every, how many times, until when.

times.description: Number of times the part is carried out.

until.description: When repeats stop, as text, for open-ended repeats ("until native cover exceeds 50%").

Recurrence.title: Recurrence

ReportingLevelEnum.description: Whose costs: the action's own, a share of a program's, or of an organization's. In the identity key.
ReportingLevelEnum.title: ReportingLevelEnum

ReversibilityEnum.description: Whether removing the cause undoes the effect. Central to restoration ecology where hysteresis and alternative stable states are key concerns.
ReversibilityEnum.title: ReversibilityEnum

ScaledValue.description: A value on a source's own ordinal or categorical scale: DFO's High / Medium / Low priority, a USDA tolerance rating, a wetland indicator status. `value` is the source's wording, verbatim. `scale` is the IRI of a SKOS scheme in vocab/scales.yaml (scale:dfo-recovery-priority, never the bare token), and `concept` the IRI of the value inside it, so "medium" can be compared with "high" without a script knowing the order (decision D18). A practitioner's "wet" is on no scale: it has a value and nothing else.

concept.description: IRI of the value inside the scheme. Optional only while a scheme is still unregistered.

scale.description: IRI of the scale's SKOS concept scheme (vocab/scales.yaml).

ScaledValue.title: ScaledValue

ScopeEnum.description: What a claim is about, following Vogt's semantic unit types. Replaces TokenTypeEnum for new records. Values and definitions must match WARP's SemanticUnitScopeEnum, so that ingestion copies them unchanged.
ScopeEnum.title: ScopeEnum

SeasonEnum.description: A season during which an effect was observed or measured. The four cardinal seasons map to NCIT, which defines them astronomically (equinox to solstice); the sub-seasons take their cardinal season as a broad mapping, because no ontology checked carries them as terms. Growing and dormant season are included because sources in strongly seasonal systems report by those rather than by calendar season. A window spanning seasons or years is not a season: record it in time_since_intervention_text or duration_text instead.
SeasonEnum.title: SeasonEnum

SemanticUnitScopeEnum.description: The scope of what a statement asserts, following Vogt's semantic unit types for statement units. Scope is part of a proposition's identity: "X reduced Y on this plot" and "X typically reduces Y" are different propositions. Definitions below are working glosses and must be checked against Vogt's own definitions before release.
SemanticUnitScopeEnum.title: SemanticUnitScopeEnum

SignificanceEnum.description: Whether the source reported this relationship as statistically significant. Separate from causal_language, which records how strongly the text commits causally, and from negated, which encodes a null result: a finding can be non-significant without the authors asserting that no relationship holds. The two non-verdict values matter as much as the verdicts, because without them an evidence gap map cannot tell "tested and not significant" from "never tested".
SignificanceEnum.title: SignificanceEnum

SiteDefinition.description: One piece of ground: the place a strategy is carried out, or whose condition is assessed. A node, so any group can point at it, but unlike every other node a particular, not a kind of thing (decisions D7, D11). Its ID is under site:, never node:, and it is written to OWL as a named individual in project/sites.ttl, typed by its ecosystem types, with its label and jurisdiction. Geometry never goes into a generated output. Checked by scripts/check_sites.py.

area_source.description: Whether the area was reported or computed.

care.description: Governance metadata: private agreements and Indigenous lands need it from the first record.

depth.description: A refinement (templates' `refinements`): the depth interval the node is about, e.g. 0 to 15 cm. Part of what the node is, but with no ontology class, so the node is a subclass of the template's expression rather than equivalent to it. Only for templates that list it (quality_of_environmental_material).

ecosystem_type.description: ENVO environmental system classes; mixed sites are common. Exported as rdf:type: the site is an instance of each.

fillers.description: One filler per template variable. Required for class_expression templates (checked by scripts/expand_nodes.py); strategies and sites have no variables.

geometry.description: GeoJSON or WKT, or a reference to one. May be generalized or withheld under care. GeoJSON must parse as JSON. Never exported.

geometry_precision.description: exact, generalized, centroid, or withheld (then no geometry at all).

jurisdiction.description: An ISO 3166-2 code (CA-SK) where one exists, exported as an IRI; or text where none does, as for many Indigenous territories, exported as a literal.

label.description: The site's name as the source gives it.

season.description: A refinement: the season the node is about ("growing season", "spring freshet"). As for depth.

specified_in.description: Plan documents that specify what was, or is to be, done: a recovery strategy, a restoration plan, a work order. Referenced by id, not inlined. Used by strategies and implementation statements.

template.description: Id of a template in templates/node_templates.yaml.

tenure.description: public, private, indigenous, mixed or unknown.

SiteDefinition.title: SiteDefinition

SourceDocument.description: Bibliographic metadata and study-level context for the source document. Supports RAG retrieval, evidence gap map construction, and spatiotemporal analysis of the evidence base. Spatial fields enable map-based evidence visualization and proximity-weighted retrieval. Temporal fields enable tracking of when evidence was collected and whether causal relationships vary over time.

document_id.description: Local identifier for this document within the graph. Use the DOI where one exists.

doi.description: Digital Object Identifier for the source document.

is_sampling_effort_reported.description: Whether the study reported its sampling effort at all. False is informative: it downgrades certainty rather than leaving a silent gap.

journal.description: Journal or publication venue for the source document.

pmid.description: PubMed identifier for the source document.

sample_size_unit.description: The unit associated with sample_size_value. Recommended best practice is a controlled vocabulary.

sample_size_value.description: The numeric value of the sample size or sampling effort reported by the study. Must have a corresponding sample_size_unit.

sampling_effort_protocol.description: A description of, or reference to, the methods used to determine the reported sampling effort. Distinct from the survey method itself.

study_coordinates.description: Coordinate set or sets reported for the study. Use one entry per reported centroid or bounded study area. This supports multi-site studies without requiring site names that the source may not report. Coordinates enable map-based evidence gap maps, proximity-weighted retrieval ("show me evidence from sites near mine"), and spatial analysis of where causal relationships have been tested.

study_country.description: Country or countries where the study was conducted. Use country names or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes where practical. If multiple countries are reported, separate them with semicolons.

study_design.description: Study design classification for EGM quality assessment.

study_duration_months.description: Duration of the study in months. Computed from start/end if both are provided, or entered directly if the paper reports duration without specific dates. Useful for filtering: "show me only studies with at least 24 months of monitoring."

study_period_end.description: End date of data collection. Same format as study_period_start.

study_period_start.description: Start date of data collection. Not the publication date — when the fieldwork or measurements actually began. ISO 8601 format. Can be year-only (2015), year-month (2015-06), or full date (2015-06-15). For paleontological or historical ecology studies, use negative years or descriptive text in study_temporal_note.

study_state_or_province.description: State, province, territory, or comparable administrative region where the study was conducted. If multiple regions are reported, separate them with semicolons.

study_temporal_note.description: Free-text note for temporal context that doesn't fit structured fields. E.g., "data collected over three growing seasons", "historical records from 1850-1950", "pollen core spanning 6,700 years."

SourceDocument.title: SourceDocument

StateOrChangeQualifierEnum.description: Qualifier indicating the state or change in the variable's attribute. Corresponds to ELMO's direction_qualifier slot. Together with measured_attribute and the entity ontology term, forms the full semantic content of a node: "state or change qualifier of attribute of entity."
StateOrChangeQualifierEnum.title: StateOrChangeQualifierEnum

Statement.description: A claim of purported truth as made by a particular agent, on a particular occasion. Statements may be used to simply put forth a possible fact (i.e. a 'proposition') as true, or to provide a more nuanced assessment of the level of confidence or evidence supporting a particular proposition.

contributions.description: Specific actions taken by an Agent toward the creation, modification, validation, or deprecation of an Information Entity.

dateAuthored.description: Indicates when the information content expressed in the Information Entity was generated.

derivedFrom.description: Another Information Entity from which this Information Entity is derived, in whole or in part.

description.description: A free text description of the Entity.

direction.description: A term indicating whether the Statement supports, disputes, or remains neutral w.r.t. the validity of the Proposition it evaluates.

extensions.description: A list of extensions to the Entity, that allow for capture of information not directly supported by elements defined in the model.

hasEvidence.description: A piece of information that represents or contributes to an argument for or against the validity of the Proposition put forth in a Statement. This is a shortcut relation that links a Statement directly to a piece of evidence supporting it, bypassing the Evidence Line class when used data creators do not utilize an Evidence Line object.

hasEvidenceFromSources.description: An Information Entity (typically a publication, dataset, or database) that provided information used as evidence to generate the knowledge expressed in a Statement.

hasEvidenceLines.description: An evidence-based argument that supports or disputes the validity of the proposition that a Statement assesses or puts forth as true. The strength and direction of this argument (whether it supports or disputes  the proposition, and how strongly) is based on an interpretation of one or more pieces of information as evidence (i.e. 'Evidence Items).

TemporalExtent.description:
The temporal window over which a causal effect was observed or measured. Distinct from the study period (when was fieldwork done): this captures the timescale of the causal relationship itself. For example, a study conducted from 2015-2020 might report that invasive removal led to native recovery "within three growing seasons" — the study period is 5 years, but the temporal extent of the causal effect is 3 growing seasons (~18 months).
This is important for practitioners who need to know how long to wait for results, and for meta-analysts investigating whether effect sizes vary with observation duration.

duration_months.description: Duration of the observed causal effect in months. E.g., 36 for "within three years", 6 for "one growing season."

duration_text.description: How long the effect lasted, as stated in the source. E.g., "within three growing seasons", "over a 20-year period", "immediately following treatment." This slot is about the effect's duration only: when the measurement was taken belongs in time_since_intervention_text, the seasons it was observed in belong in observation_seasons, and the study's own fieldwork dates belong in source_document.

lag_months.description: Time lag between the cause and the onset of the effect, in months. E.g., if invasive removal happens in year 0 and native recovery begins in year 2, lag = 24. Null if the effect is immediate or lag is not reported.

observation_grain.description: The temporal grain at which the effect was measured. E.g., "daily", "monthly", "seasonal", "annual", "decadal." Affects interpretability — a relationship detected at annual grain may not hold at daily grain.

observation_seasons.description: Seasons during which the effect was observed, where it is seasonally restricted, e.g. [late_spring, summer]. Important for context-dependent effects that may not hold year-round. A window that spans seasons or years is not a season: record it in time_since_intervention_text or duration_text.

time_since_intervention_months.description: Elapsed time between the intervention, or the onset of the driver, and the measurement this edge reports, in months. "in year 2" is 24; "six years after establishing the experiment" is 72. Distinct from duration_months, which is how long the effect lasted, and from lag_months, which is how long it took to begin. Where a reading spans a window, give its end. This is the slot that lets readings from one study be ordered into a trajectory.

time_since_intervention_text.description: The measurement epoch as the source states it, e.g. "in year 2", "by the second growing season", "results at year 3 of the experiment". Use alongside time_since_intervention_months, and alone where the source is too vague to convert.

response_curve.description: Habitat suitability breakpoints, in order: x strictly increasing (checked by scripts/check_tolerance.py), suitability in [0, 1], x in the unit of `range`. A model's combination rule (geometric mean, minimum) is not a statement: record it on the EcoStudyResult.
